text: This is the solicitor side of Metis Cortex, running live in production.
That was a client conference. This is what Metis makes of it.

These two fields are mandatory. Sewell versus Zelden: the risks the solicitor warned of, and how the client responded. Those two decide negligence and complaint outcomes. Metis cannot produce a brief without them, and where the conversation did not contain them, it says so rather than inventing something.
It searches Ostley during the conference. Seventeen findings here, and against current law: note the post May twenty twenty four parenting framework, not the old one.

Conflict check and client identification, dated and retained. The costs disclosure works out its own tier from the estimate. But the four section one seven four rights statements are deliberately left blank.
Nothing reaches the client until the solicitor approves it. The A.I. draft stays invisible to them until a human signs off.
One honest note: the transcript in this recording was pasted in. The audio path is built, and it is consent gated under the Surveillance Devices Act. That needs a human click, by design.
It is built and it works. It is not open to firms yet, because that costs disclosure wording needs a solicitor's sign off.
